label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition, early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never at D1 or GO), and only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1, i.e. a rare transition (in_action=2, in_state=1 together cover 99.9% of activations). This is an input-conjunction detector. It is also gated strongly by episode time: the rate is about 5% in trials 0-29, near zero from trial 30 to 89, with a small return in trials 90-99. Without the time term the predicate reaches recall 0.999 but precision 0.21. Adding ep_trial < 25 gives dev P 0.87 / R 0.89 / F1 0.88 / mass recall 0.95, and the remaining misses are mostly weak activations in trials 25-35. Magnitude is largest on a2->S1 rare transitions inside windows that have had several rare transitions, while S2 is good (choice logit strongly favours a2, value in the 7.1-7.5 band). It does not fire on a1->S2 rare transitions, on common transitions, or at D1/GO. All variables used are observed at D2.

issues: All the main claims hold up on dev data. Every activation is at D2, with none at D1 or GO. in_action=2 together with in_state=1 covers 99.9% of activations (11594 of 11604). The unit never fires when in_state=2, so it never fires on a1->S2 rare transitions, and it fires on common transitions only 10 times. At D2, the predicate ~(a2 & S1) has recall 0.0009.
Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.846 / R 0.895 / F1 0.870 / mass recall 0.954.

Small inaccuracy in the time description. The firing rate by bin is 4.9% (trials 0-9), 4.3% (10-19) and 1.9% (20-29). So 'about 5% in trials 0-29' overstates the 20-29 bin. The return in trials 90-99 (0.5% rate, 3% of activation mass) is real but diffuse. Adding ep_trial>=98 to the predicate lowers test F1 to 0.859.

Misses: actives in trials 25-35 make up 6.8% of actives but only 2.1% of activation mass, which is consistent with 'weak activations in trials 25-35'. Another 4.6% of actives fall at ep_trial>=36, mostly in trials 90-99.

There are false positives early in the episode on a2->S1 steps where S1 is good or the agent has just switched from a1. Adding good, choice, prev_action or value conditions does not raise F1 in a meaningful way (best is the value band 7.0-7.75, dev F1 0.884 against 0.877), so no systematic counterexample class remains.

The predicate uses no future variables. 'S2 is good' and 'value 7.1-7.5' correctly describe where the largest activations sit (good=2 carries 68% of activation mass; the value bin 7.13-7.54 carries 84%), but they are not needed in the predicate.
